🌍 Pezeshkian meets with senior managers of American media

📌 New York, IRNA — President Masoud Pezeshkian has met with editors-in-chief and senior officials of US media outlets.

During the meeting in New York on Thursday morning local time, Pezeshkian explained Iran’s views and engaged in a candid discussion with the editors-in-chief and senior media officials, responding to their various questions.
​
The meeting was held as part of the Iranian president’s bilateral meetings and side events on the sidelines of the 81st United Nations General Assembly.
​
Pezeshkian arrived at John F. Kennedy International Airport early Wednesday, where he was received by Iran’s ambassador and chargé d’affaires to the United Nations.

🔊 Iran reacts firmly to inappropriate language by Australian envoy at UNHRC

📌 London, IRNA – The representative of Iran at the UN Human Rights Council has reacted strongly to inappropriate language used by an Australian representative against Iran.

In reaction to the Australian representative, when she referred to the Islamic Republic of Iran as a “regime” in his remarks on Thursday at the 20th meeting of the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council, the Iranian representative raised a point of order, emphasizing the importance of adhering to diplomatic norms and using the official names of UN member states.
​
Addressing the Vice President of the session, she said, “My delegation wishes to draw attention to the matter of procedural and diplomatic concern regarding the language used in this Chamber. Within the United Nations, Member States are expected to address one another in accordance with established norms of diplomatic propriety and mutual respect, including the use of official state names.”
​
She added, “The deliberate substitution of such names with politically charged or projective terminology, such as the term ‘regime,’ is inconsistent with the spirit, decorum, and rules of conduct of the governing of this Council. My delegation, therefore, respectfully calls upon you, Mr. Vice President, to uphold the standard of this Assembly. The delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran wishes to draw the attention of this meeting to an important issue, from both a procedural and diplomatic perspective, concerning the language used in this chamber.”
​
The Iranian representative said, “At the United Nations, member states are expected to address one another in accordance with accepted standards of diplomatic courtesy and mutual respect. The use of countries’ official names is part of these standards.”

🔊 Araghchi criticizes European countries for ignoring US violations of international law

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has criticized European countries, including Germany, for ignoring US violations of international law and acts of bullying.

Araghchi and Wadephul held talks on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.
​
The top Iranian diplomat outlined Tehran’s positions on international developments, stressing that restoring confidence in the United Nations requires all countries to adhere to the principles and purposes of the UN Charter and international law.
​
Araghchi also pointed to the ongoing occupation and warmongering by the Israeli regime in West Asia, describing the arms and political support provided by Germany and some other European countries as a significant factor in the continuation of the regime’s crimes against countries in the region. He emphasized the importance of ending this complicity in these crimes, putting an end to impunity, and holding the occupying regime accountable.
​
Additionally, he underscored Iran’s commitment to pursuing diplomacy regarding its peaceful nuclear program, stressing that no party can ignore Iran’s good faith in the negotiations, as well as the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran in the midst of the talks, while portraying Iran as responsible for insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz.
​
Araghchi stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran has conveyed to the American side its reasonable conditions and requirements for advancing diplomacy, emphasizing that restoring security to the region requires an end to US interventionist and aggressive actions against Iran.
​
The two sides also discussed issues of mutual ties as well as the two countries’ diplomatic and consular consultations.
